figures.caption: Fig. 3: Layer-wise VDEpre, VDEpost, and downstream accuracy across five image benchmarks for Video-LLaVA (CLIP) and LLaVA-Video (SigLIP). Curves are averaged over five random seeds using 100 samples per seed. The dashed vertical line indicates the default visual layer used by each model.
Table 1: Preliminary finding: the vision backbone’s default layer is often sub-optimal.

Fig. 2: Layer-wise visual representation profiling on ScienceQA. VDE is estimated from 100 sampled examples over five seeds and compared with exhaustive layer-wise downstream accuracy. GW distances measure the structural compatibility between visual and question-side language representations.

Table 3: Top-3 candidate layer retrieval. Hits denote whether the oracle best layer is covered by the Top-3 layers ranked by VDEpre or VDEpost. Pre/Post Top-1 vs. Best Acc. compares Top-1 VDE-selected accuracy with oracle best accuracy. Bold entries mark covered oracle layers or exact Top-1 matches.

Fig. 1: Overview of the proposed visual-layer profiling framework. Two training-free geometric signals are computed across candidate layers: VDE, measured from pre- and post-projector visual representations, and GW, measuring visual-language structural alignment. Both are profiled against downstream layer usefulness to assess how well each predicts strong visual layers.

Fig. 4: Layer-wise profiling results on HD-EPIC Action Recognition. We perform a full-layer scan using 50 sampled examples with one random seed. The figure compares VDEpre, VDEpost, downstream accuracy, and GW-based cross-modal alignment across visual layers for the evaluated video VLMs.

Fig. 5: Layer-wise profiling results on HD-EPIC Gaze Estimation. We use five random seeds with 100 sampled examples and restrict the scan to the mid-to-high visual layers. The figure compares VDEpre, VDEpost, and downstream accuracy across visual layers for the evaluated video VLMs.
